item.title: Law enforcement agencies tackle removing wrecked, abandoned boats
item.description: The Tipsea Gypsea lies beached on a sandbar, two anchor lines extending from the bow of the 45-foot sailboat.On the hull, a bright orange sticker has been placed declaring the vessel must be removed. The 1989 Catalina sits just a few hundred feet from the Harbor Acres neighborhood on Sarasota Bay and on the outskirts of the Marina Jack mooring field where dozens of boats are anchored. item.title: Air taxis: An alternative to sitting in Longboat Key's traffic jams?
item.description: “Flying cars, they said."That’s a common online punchline about the lack of technological advancement since shows like The Jetsons predicted a space utopia where flying cars were commonplace vehicles for commuters. Instead, all we get is AI videos of cats whitewater rafting.But now, sci-fi is becoming reality. item.title: Longboat's Spanish Main looks for normalcy a year after the storms
item.description: The rebuild continues at Spanish Main Yacht Club, one of the hardest hit communities from the 2024 hurricanes.Sixteen months after storm surge from Hurricane Helene flooded Longboat Key, contractors are still spotted routinely coming in and out of the community. item.title: Cursive writing requirements would change if proposed legislation passes
item.description: Lakewood Ranch's Mark Eubanks, a sixth grader at Dan R. Nolan Middle, has memorized how to write his signature in cursive. item.title: Marian Anderson property redevelopment plan advances
item.description: The transformation of a long-blighted brownfield site owned by the city of Sarasota in Newtown has advanced another step as the City Commission, on second reading, unanimously approved a land use designation change on the property.At their Feb. 2 meeting, commissioners put their final stamp on a future land use category change of 9.22 acres, at what is called the Marian Anderson site, from Community Commercial to Production Intensive Commercial.
